assumptions.text: IdealMac at each delivery: a tag verifies only if it was minted for exactly that claim, in every state.
assumptions.real_world: No real signature or MAC scheme with a total verifier meets it in every state (U478; Attack.TotalVerifierBreaksIdealMac; TotalReading.NoIdealMac).

assumptions.text: A2_MintOnlyOnCheck: every mint of one of our ids signs CheckedClaim(pre, t) for some pre, t with Authorizes(pre, t).
assumptions.real_world: The issuer (ts/refund-finality/minter.ts) signs only after the compiled RefundFinality.Check returns true. minter.ts is TESTED only.

assumptions.text: A5: the sink's sigOk boolean equals the model's VerifyTag on the delivered token at each delivery.
assumptions.real_world: sink.ts calls Ed25519 verify on exactly the bytes that the model calls the claim. Decomposed (RepairedBytes) into H3b, H3c, B5, H3d-B6 and the trace-local A4-NOCOLL-RUN; H3a is retired.

assumptions.text: H1_SignatureAuthenticity (claim level, step-local): a delivered token whose tag verifies carries a claim signed earlier.
assumptions.real_world: Ed25519 EUF-CMA AND secrecy of the signing key; holds up to a negligible forgery probability, only while the key is secret.

assumptions.text: H1B_ByteUnforgeability: byte string and tag that verify were signed earlier (symbolic EUF-CMA at byte level).
assumptions.real_world: Same as H1, stated on bytes; with H3b/H3c/B5/H3d-B6/A4-NOCOLL-RUN it gives H1 and A5 (RepairedBytes.RepairedGiveClaimAuthenticity).

assumptions.text: H3a: the claim serialization is injective (on model claims that carry the full pre-state).
assumptions.real_world: FALSE for the real token: the token carries only SHA-256 of the pre-state, so two pre-states with one hash give one byte string (ByteAttacks.PreStateCollisionBreaksApprovedSpec; ByteAttacks.HashedPreSerNotInjective). RETIRED.
assumptions.retired_reason: False for the real token (hash of the pre-state only).

assumptions.text: H3b: at each delivery the sink rebuilds exactly Ser(ClaimOf(tok)) from the parsed token.
assumptions.real_world: sink.ts rebuilds the signed bytes; not proved.

assumptions.text: H3c: the model VerifyTag is the byte verifier applied to Ser(claim).
assumptions.real_world: A definition choice of the model; no real-world content beyond H3a and B5.

assumptions.text: B5: the crypto layer boolean is the byte verifier on the rebuilt bytes.
assumptions.real_world: Node OpenSSL Ed25519 verify returns the mathematical verifier value.

assumptions.text: A3: Commit is one atomic, durable step.
assumptions.real_world: One SQLite transaction in node:sqlite. Process crash: TESTED (486 kills, 0 violations, worker run). Power loss: SQLite defaults, no full fsync.

assumptions.text: A4 faithful state: comparing state hashes equals comparing states.
assumptions.real_world: SHA-256 collision resistance and a canonical state encoding.

assumptions.text: A6: the artifact computes the flat contract on ALL FlatIn inputs (any Unicode chars).
assumptions.real_world: The HOL side gives the flat contract only for byte strings (chars < 256) (Orchestrator A, 08:03Z). Not met by the M1 artifact as stated.

assumptions.text: A6b_ArtifactComputesFlatContractOnBytes: the artifact computes the flat contract on byte-string inputs.
assumptions.real_world: The M1 executable on byte inputs computes the flat contract. Equivalent in Dafny to A6x (SliceFromExport.A6xIffA6b). Needs X1 to X10 and A7-ART: open.

assumptions.text: InitOk: the protocol starts in the initial state of the model.
assumptions.real_world: A fresh store.

assumptions.text: GoodStart: the store that the patched core serves satisfies the core invariant at start (fresh, or AuditStart passes).
assumptions.real_world: A start-up audit (AuditStart, executable) runs before the core serves an old store. It gives structural facts only: AttackCore.GoodStartDoesNotBoundMoney (a store passing the audit holds a refund of 500 on an original of 100). Not deployed.

assumptions.text: A4_NoCollisionInRun (trace-local): for each mint and each delivery of ONE trace, equal hashes of the two pre-states imply equal pre-states (and the same for the two id hashes).
assumptions.real_world: SHA-256 collision resistance on the pairs of one run; holds except with negligible probability; global injectivity is NOT needed (RepairedBytes).

assumptions.text: A4b_NoStoredStateCollision: the real sink compares the stored state with the token by SHA-256 of the canonical state text; equal hashes imply equal states.
assumptions.real_world: The real token carries only preStateSha256. Same collision argument as A4-NOCOLL-RUN, a second time, in the sink. Used by NO proof (named in RepairedBytes only).

assumptions.text: H3d_MintsParseable and B6_DeliveriesParseable: every minted claim and every delivered token parses under the canonical token grammar of SerModel.
assumptions.real_world: minter.ts builds only canonical bodies; sink.ts rejects non-canonical text (TESTED: 443 bodies, b-ser conformance). Not proved for the TypeScript.

assumptions.text: Every trace lemma (L0 to L3, several charges) starts from the EMPTY store; a restart from a non-empty store is covered only as one trace from the empty store.
assumptions.real_world: A deployed sink restarts on an existing database; no restart lemma exists (b-restart running at generation time). Scope limit, not a fact about the world.

assumptions.text: WellKeyed / KeyedInits: no two databases (charge stores) hold one charge id.
assumptions.real_world: NOT enforced by the model, sink.ts or the dispatcher; AttackMulti.NotWellKeyedDoubleRefund: one token commits in two databases. Needs a creation rule for charge keys.

assumptions.text: BETA-VALUES: Dafny int and HOL int are both the mathematical integers; Dafny bool and HOL bool agree; a Dafny string whose chars are < 256 and the HOL string with the same code list denote the same value.
assumptions.real_world: ARGUED, not proved (two tools, no common semantics): b-export-bridge/BRIDGE_STATEMENT.md section 2; Orchestrator A FIELDS_FOR_B.md.

assumptions.text: BETA-OPS: each of the nine export forms (Eq on bool/int/string, Neq, And, Or, Imp, Le, Not) and three literal forms has the same reading in Dafny (as written by gen_exported.py) and in the HOL Dafny semantics.
assumptions.real_world: ARGUED by a table of source line references (BRIDGE_STATEMENT.md section 2); gen_exported.py is an unproved reader cross-checked by a second reader (Mirror.dfy trees equal).

assumptions.text: BETA-ORDER: the export names bind the same argument and tuple positions on both sides (charge, request, original, remaining, enabled, opened, candidate, amount, reason).
assumptions.real_world: ARGUED: a charge/request swap on BOTH sides is invisible to both proofs (contract symmetric); a one-sided swap fails (A: NB1 go exit 1). BRIDGE_STATEMENT.md section 3.

assumptions.text: A6x_ArtifactMeetsExportedContractOnBytes: the artifact flat function meets the three exported clauses on byte-string inputs.
assumptions.real_world: A hypothesis in Dafny; equivalent to A6b (A6xIffA6b). Real-world reading needs A7-ART and the HOL chain X1 to X10.

assumptions.text: A7-ART: the artifact function of the Dafny lemma is the HOL function refund_fields, and the run-time bytes are the UTF-8 encodings of its string fields.
assumptions.real_world: Names one function on two sides; no tool relates them (U539). The executable computes refund_fields only through X1 to X10 (open).

assumptions.text: OS process contract of the launcher: the OS delivers the complete stdout of a terminated child, reports a signal or exit status truthfully, and enforces the launcher timeout.
assumptions.real_world: macOS process and pipe semantics; trusted. CE-1 and CE-2 (exit 0 with truncated or empty stdout) show why exit status alone is not success.
